summary: Round r1 (restricted network): 41 external variables that the shared model needs (derived from the 17 non-projection transmission channels in src/geopolitical_model/channels.py, the 20-entry exposure register and the 50 subagent specifications of Agents 17-26) are each assigned to a primary supplying subagent, supporting subagents and a domestic counterpart, and mapped to primary source ids in the source catalog (tier-1 Nepal official first). Every one of the 50 Division-B subagents 17A-26E has at least one assigned variable. Document-level source leads were located by web search for the variables with identifiable primary tables; no values were retrieved, so every empirical item is pending. Key coordination risks: fiscal-year vs calendar-year mixing (NRB, DoFE, customs, PDMO on Nepal FY; KNOMAD, WDI, IDS, UNCTAD, tourism arrivals, BIS on calendar year), coverage gaps (DoFE excludes India-bound migrants; NRB may under-record ICT exports), and three 2026 developments reported in search results that bear on scenarios S01, S05 and S08 and must be verified from primary documents before use.

findings.claim: External-variable list for the shared model: 41 variables mapped to channels and model variables (see specific.global_task_list). This is a research-design output, not an empirical value.

Primary-source assignment per variable follows the catalog hierarchy (Nepal official > IMF/WB/ADB > UN > foreign governments > energy authorities > ICIMOD/climate > academic); see specific.source_assignments.

All empirical external inputs (remittances, migrant stocks, trade shares, fuel prices, debt composition, FDI by source, tourism arrivals, electricity trade, interest rates, exchange rates) remain unretrieved in r1.
findings.note: Requires `python -m src.cli leads --fetch` for the lead URLs listed in source_leads, then extraction and ingest-csv in r2.

findings.claim: Monthly or quarterly versions of every calendar-year international series (commodity prices, policy rates, INR/USD, partner GDP) are needed to re-aggregate to Nepal FY (mid-July to mid-July); annual calendar-year values cannot be used directly.
findings.note: Monthly series from IMF PCPS, Fed H.15, RBI DBIE; quarterly partner GDP where available.

findings.claim: Three 2026 developments surfaced by search that may alter scenario status: (a) a Middle East conflict from early 2026 affecting Gulf labour markets, aviation and remittances (World Bank Nepal Development Update April 2026, IMF 2026 Article IV); (b) Nepal's request under the UN CDP Crisis Response Process to extend the LDC preparatory period (CDP Crisis Assessment July 2026); (c) an August 2026 cross-border debris flood at Rasuwagadhi-Kerung (ICIMOD). None is yet recorded as an observation.
findings.note: Retrieve leads L47, L48, L52, L34 and record dated event observations before any scenario use.

data_gaps: No document-level lead yet for: RBI/Fed monthly series extraction formats, UN DESA International Migrant Stock (not in source catalog), GCC host-country statistics by nationality beyond GLMM, IATA/OAG seat data (not in catalog, likely licensed), China customs data on trade with Nepal, MoF Development Cooperation Report (grants/ODA by donor).
Variables X33, X35, X36, X37, X39, X40 have no located primary lead in r1; supplying agents must locate them.

Engine coverage: only aggregate_real_growth, domestic_prices and exchange_rate have projection_variable in channels.py; the other external variables can only be carried as structured qualitative transmission records until modules exist.
Source catalog lacks ids for: World Bank Commodity Markets (Pink Sheet), ILO reports (as opposed to ILOSTAT), ITC, UN DESA migrant stock, IATA/OAG, Indian DGFT notifications, China GACC customs.

assumptions.text: The list of external variables is derived from channels.py model_variables, the exposure register and the Agent 17-26 specifications; variables required only by domestic agents are out of scope for 16A.

Where a channel has several owners, the Division-B subagent with the matching research focus is designated primary supplier; domestic owners in channels.py are recorded as domestic counterparts that convert the input into model form.

Calendar-year international series enter the model only after documented conversion to Nepal FY using monthly/quarterly data; annual-to-FY interpolation is a fallback that must be labelled as an estimate method.
News articles and secondary platforms (e.g. CEIC, Trading Economics, newspapers) are used only to find primary documents and are never cited for values.

challenges.text: channels.py owner lists omit several Division-B suppliers (e.g. remittances channel lacks 19D; fuel_prices lacks 21D; tourism_demand lacks 19C; external_financing lacks 25D/26E). Suggest reconciling owners with specific.global_task_list; 16A does not edit platform code.

Source catalog lacks ids for World Bank Commodity Markets (Pink Sheet), ITC, ILO reports, UN DESA International Migrant Stock, China customs (GACC) and Indian DGFT notifications; leads citing them carry source_id null until catalogued.

DoFE labour approvals exclude India-bound migrants and irregular migration; migrant stock by destination must combine DoFE flows with Census 2021 absentee data and host-country statistics, keeping each value separate.

Tourism arrivals by nationality are calendar-year; NRB travel receipts are Nepal FY. Do not compute receipts per arrival or shares across the two bases without conversion. Also verify coverage of Indian land arrivals in arrival statistics.

Reported disagreement between NRB-recorded ICT/BPO service receipts and industry claims (payments possibly recorded as remittances). Keep both, document classification rules (BPM6 services vs secondary income) and escalate to 00B if the gap exceeds tolerance.
PDMO reports central-government external debt on Nepal FY/monthly; World Bank IDS reports total external debt (public and private) on calendar-year end. Reconcile coverage before comparing.

Escalation: search results indicate 2026 developments (Middle East conflict, LDC-graduation extension request, Rasuwagadhi-Kerung flood) that may change the status or calibration of S01, S05, S08 and S10. Pending verification from leads L34, L47, L48, L52.

Escalation for red-team review: the same 2026 developments and the variable-to-agent assignment should be tested for missing channels (e.g. food-staple export restrictions, northern border closure, remittance-channel concentration), which 16B proposes as new exposure entries.

uncertainty: High. No external variable has a retrieved observation in r1; the assignment table is a research design whose completeness depends on the channel registry, which itself lacks engine support for most channels. Lead URLs were identified by web search and some may have moved or be incomplete (e.g. the latest customs annual book and DoFE yearly reports were not located as direct files). The 2026 developments are reported only in search results and secondary sources and must be treated as unverified.
